summary.intent: Recover the Phase 37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) planning work that was discussed in a prior session but never committed, then create context and plans for the phase.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 context was captured via discuss-phase workflow with all key architectural decisions locked, followed by full research and planning that produced 2 PLAN.md files across 2 waves, verified and committed.

repo: Phase 37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) was added to ROADMAP.md and its directory created in a prior session but never committed — the artifacts existed only as unstaged local changes.

The current upload pipeline in useDropUpload.ts:113-133 loops sequentially, with each file calling client.uploadFile() which does encrypt → IPFS pin → add FilePointer → publish folder IPNS — resulting in N IPNS publishes for N files.
The SDK's withOperation() serializer means concurrent calls to uploadFile() would just queue, making Option C (parallelizing at web layer with existing API) non-viable without SDK changes.

Desktop FUSE upload model is fundamentally different from web: files arrive one-at-a-time via release() callbacks, so the Rust SDK cannot benefit from batch uploads without a separate write-coalescing architecture layer.

Stale-children race condition exists in batch upload: if another device publishes folder children via sync during the encrypt+pin window, a naive batch publish would overwrite them — mitigation is re-read folder metadata just before final publish.
Memory spike risk if all files encrypt concurrently before any are pinned — must pipeline as encrypt→pin→free→next slot rather than encrypt-all→pin-all.

code.finding: Sequential file upload loop — each iteration calls client.uploadFile() which includes its own IPNS publish, causing N publishes for N files.
uploadFile() is an atomic unit doing encrypt+pin+publish, wrapped in withOperation() serializer — makes concurrent calls impossible without new batch API.
FUSE release() callback handles per-file upload individually — no batch context available at this layer, making write-coalescing a separate architectural concern.
Rust SDK upload queue confirms desktop processes files individually via queue, not in batches.

workflow: The discuss-phase workflow in assumptions mode first does deep codebase analysis via a gsd-assumptions-analyzer subagent, surfaces assumptions with evidence and confidence, then asks the user only to correct what's wrong — resulting in ~4 targeted interactions vs 15-20 questions.
When a usage limit interrupts a subagent mid-workflow, spawning a fresh agent with the same prompt and context is the recovery path.

The plan-phase workflow writes a VALIDATION.md strategy file from research output before spawning the planner, then verifies plans with gsd-plan-checker and auto-fixes minor warnings before presenting results.
